memory_update.text: PLPC should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a US-listed underfollowed transmission-hardware candidate, but its exact exposure to high-voltage/HVDC-related projects needs filing-level verification.
AMSC is the cleanest US-listed small/mid-cap mapping found for grid power-quality and renewable interconnection systems through D-VAR STATCOM and Gridtec Solutions.
POWL is an adjacent electrical-equipment candidate for medium-voltage switchgear and power-control infrastructure; include but tag as less direct to HVDC reactors.
The US-listed universe appears stronger for adjacent transmission hardware, STATCOM/reactive power, switchgear, and utility components than for direct HVDC reactor suppliers.

Direct HVDC reactor exposure likely requires a non-US or private/OEM supplier search, including India, Europe, Japan, Korea, and transformer/reactor component suppliers; Quality Power Electrical Equipments remains a non-US lead requiring primary-source verification.

node: High-voltage reactors, HVDC components, grid power-quality systems, and renewable-integration equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the high-voltage / grid power-quality node with a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: Hubbell as a broader, better-known utility-equipment context anchor. Underfollowed lane: PLPC, AMSC, and POWL, each with plausible direct or second-order exposure to transmission hardware, STATCOM/reactive-power systems, medium-voltage switchgear, and renewable/grid interconnection equipment. No candidate here is confirmed as a pure HVDC-reactor supplier; that specific sub-node still appears more likely to require non-US listings or private/OEM supply-chain mapping. This pass treats US-listed candidates as adjacent chokepoint exposures rather than direct proof of HVDC reactor bottleneck capture.
